title: THE SPOON’S NEW OFFICE
text: You discover that dropping a spoon makes {{carer}} fetch it. The office has no salary, but excellent powers.

outcome.text: {{carer}} retrieves it, then moves the bowl beyond your jurisdiction.
{{carer}} accepts the damp gift with ceremony. You have invented an inefficient but pleasant form of cooperation.

title: THE NIGHT INSPECTOR
text: {{carer}} has finally sat down. You open your eyes to check that the household remains properly staffed.

outcome.text: {{carer}} arrives with one shoe on the wrong foot. The inspection passes; the inspector remains unsatisfied.

choices.label: Settle to the sound of the chair

outcome.text: The chair creaks once more, then stops. {{carer}} gets a little rest without having to earn it twice.

title: THE FORTIFICATION OF SUPPER
text: You have arranged crusts round your bowl. {{carer}} attempts to introduce a spoon through an undefended gate.

choices.label: Defend the gate with both hands

outcome.text: The soup breaches the wall and most of your sleeve. {{carer}} admires the defence while removing the evidence.

choices.label: Let the spoon into the fortress

outcome.text: You eat. {{carer}} calls the siege a success and declines to discuss whose side won.

title: THE BOOT WITH A PASSENGER
text: You put a wooden toy inside {{carer}}’s boot. Departure now depends on a small creature accepting terms.

outcome.text: {{carer}} thanks you for solving a problem in which you have shown unusually complete expertise.

choices.label: Pretend the boot has always lived there

outcome.text: {{carer}} tips out the toy and studies your perfectly serious face. The boot resumes ordinary work.

title: THE CAT’S NEW NAME
text: You give the household cat a new name. {{carer}} asks what happened to its old one.

outcome.text: {{carer}} understands none of the explanation and all of the importance. The cat responds to neither name.
The cat leaves. {{carer}} praises your accurate imitation of an adult being ignored.

title: THE LAUNDRY HEARING
text: {{carer}} proposes washing your face. You have not been consulted about the status of the dirt.

outcome.text: You preserve one muddy cheek through extraordinary effort. {{carer}} wins the other by negotiation.
{{carer}} gives you one corner. Your face becomes cleaner and the floor rather less so.

title: THE UNRECOGNISED ANIMAL
text: You shape a piece of dough and insist it is an animal. {{carer}} guesses carefully.

outcome.text: {{carer}} finally names a creature nobody has seen. You accept the answer and eat its head.

choices.label: Give the creature to your carer

outcome.text: {{carer}} leaves it beside the hearth where it can become bread without ceasing to be important.

title: THE BLANKET EXCHANGE
text: {{carer}} offers a clean blanket for the old one. The old one knows how to be yours.

choices.label: Hold on to the familiar corner

outcome.text: {{carer}} washes the other end first. The compromise leaves you holding a small but recognised country.
The new blanket smells different. {{carer}} stays until different has stopped meaning alone.

title: THE EXTRA PERSON ON THE WALL
text: A candle makes a stranger out of {{carer}}’s shadow. The stranger appears to possess a very long nose.

outcome.text: {{carer}} bows and makes the nose longer. The stranger becomes less frightening and less dignified.
{{carer}} moves the candle. The stranger goes home without requiring you to be brave for an audience.

title: THE THREAD YOU CAN REACH
text: {{carer}} mends a sleeve while you hold the spare thread. The household has placed considerable confidence in a small fist.

outcome.text: {{carer}} finishes the stitch and thanks you as though the sleeve could not have survived without the help.

choices.label: Test whether the thread is firmly attached

outcome.text: It is not. {{carer}} starts again and gives you a shorter, less strategically important piece.

title: THE NEW HEADMASTER
text: The children elect a goat after it eats the attendance register. {{teacher}} declares the election unlawful. {{peer}} says the goat already has a carrot and three votes of confidence.

outcome.text: {{teacher}} removes the carrot from the meeting. The new headmaster follows its principal source of legitimacy out of the yard.
The goat eats the appeal. {{teacher}} concedes that its administration is unusually decisive.
You improve attendance by adding children who are not present and one unusually literate pig. {{teacher}} notices the pig first.

title: THE FINGER THAT GAVE EVIDENCE
text: {{teacher}} asks who touched the ink. {{peer}} recommends denying it before you remember which hand is black.

outcome.text: {{teacher}} gives you a cleaning cloth. The lesson begins with a remarkably well-supported confession.

choices.label: Hide the hand behind your back

outcome.text: You leave a black handprint on your tunic. {{peer}} admires evidence that can travel with its owner.

title: THE COURT WITHOUT A SECOND STOOL
text: {{peer}} holds court because their household owns the stool. The accused owns the biscuits.

choices.label: Hear the charge before the biscuits

outcome.text: The court hears an excellent case and receives no biscuits. {{peer}} asks whether justice is always this hungry.
The accused distributes the evidence. {{peer}} declares the case deliciously inconclusive.

title: THE BOAT THAT HAS NO INTEREST IN COMMAND
text: You and {{peer}} launch a wooden boat in a ditch. It immediately joins a different fleet beneath the bridge.

outcome.text: You recover the boat and lose a sleeve to the mud. {{peer}} appoints you admiral of the stick.
{{peer}} demands a refund on behalf of the spectators. The spectators are three children and one unmoved dog.

title: THE CAKE RESERVED FOR A SAINT
text: {{peer}} finds a cake set aside for the parish celebration. The saint has not yet arrived to object.

outcome.text: {{peer}} helps guard the cake. Both guards are paid in slices after the duty is over.

choices.label: Taste only enough to establish its quality

outcome.text: The testing spreads to the other side of the cake. {{peer}} suggests calling the missing part an offering.

title: THE BUTTON AT THE CENTRE OF THE WORLD
text: {{peer}} has lost a prized button in the rushes. Finding it has become more important than anything adults claim to be doing.

outcome.text: You find a bone bead, a nail and finally the button. {{peer}} keeps the button and gives you the bead.

choices.label: Claim you can find it for a reward

outcome.text: {{peer}} produces the button from another pocket before your demonstration. Your confidence remains for sale with fewer customers.

title: THE APPLE THAT DISPROVES THE SUM
text: {{teacher}} explains division using apples. {{peer}} is performing subtraction from the far end of the bench.

choices.label: Count the evidence before it vanishes

outcome.text: {{teacher}} changes the lesson to subtraction and asks {{peer}} to supply the answer. The answer is full.
The arithmetic becomes easy and the teacher becomes difficult. {{peer}} shares the last piece before the examples are confiscated.

title: THE WORD YOU WERE NOT MEANT TO LEARN
text: {{carer}} uses a splendid new word after dropping a pot. {{peer}} asks whether you can remember it.

outcome.text: {{carer}} explains that the word is not useful at chapel. {{peer}} is disappointed by such a limited application.
The word reaches three neighbours before {{carer}} reaches you. {{peer}} has acquired a favourite new quotation.

title: THE CROWN MADE OF THE WRONG HEDGE
text: {{peer}} makes a crown from a hedge nobody has first tested for thorns.

choices.label: Make a safer crown from rushes

outcome.text: {{peer}} accepts the replacement with the dignity of a ruler whose ears have recently been defeated.

choices.label: Prove it is perfectly suitable for royalty

outcome.text: You remove it quickly. {{peer}} agrees that a shorter reign can still be historic.

title: THE TOLL AT THE VERY SMALL BRIDGE
text: {{peer}} charges a pebble to cross a plank over a puddle. The bypass is one ordinary step.

outcome.text: {{peer}} announces a wider jurisdiction. You take a wider step.
The takings reach six pebbles before the owner of the plank asks for it back. {{peer}} gives you a glowing reference.

title: THE BELL THAT RINGS FOR BISCUITS
text: {{peer}} finds a small bell and proposes summoning the entire household to supper. Nobody has made supper.

choices.label: Return the bell before the announcement

outcome.text: The household remains undisturbed. {{peer}} says you have no appreciation of ceremony.
Three adults arrive with impressive speed. {{peer}} discovers that the bell does not also produce food.

title: THE INSPECTION OF THE IMPORTANT POCKET
text: {{carer}} empties your pocket before washing your clothes. The inventory includes a smooth stone, a bent nail and something that has accepted neither name nor explanation.

choices.label: Explain each treasure before sorting it

outcome.text: {{carer}} keeps the stone and removes the nail. The unidentified object is granted a hearing outside, with a shovel.
It unfolds. {{carer}} opens the door and allows your collection to leave under its own power.

title: THE LOAF WITH A JOURNEY MISSING
text: {{carer}} sends you home from the baker with a loaf. By the time you reach the door, a small section of the journey has been eaten.

choices.label: Explain where the missing piece went

outcome.text: {{carer}} cuts the loaf at the bite. Your share becomes remarkably easy to identify.

choices.label: Describe an unusually precise attack by birds

outcome.text: {{carer}} asks why the birds left teeth marks. Your evidence is returned for further preparation.

title: THE DOOR THAT RECORDS YOUR HEIGHT
text: {{carer}} marks your height on a doorpost. The previous mark is disappointingly close, considering how much work growing has been.

choices.label: Stand flat and accept the new mark

outcome.text: {{carer}} dates it carefully. There is still room above for years you cannot yet imagine.

choices.label: Improve the measurement with your heels

outcome.text: {{carer}} marks the extra height with a tiny drawing of your feet. The record is accurate in a particularly inconvenient way.

title: THE ERRAND THAT NEEDS A RECEIPT
text: {{other}} offers you a coin to carry a parcel across the square. The parcel is light; the instructions about not looking inside are unusually heavy.

choices.label: Ask who will receive it before agreeing

outcome.text: {{other}} points to the cobbler. The parcel contains a repaired shoe, and the elaborate secrecy concerns a very large hole in the other one.
{{other}} crosses the square carrying the parcel. The strange limping walk supplies an explanation you did not have to purchase.

title: THE VISITOR WHO GETS THE WARM PLACE
text: {{carer}} gives a tired visitor your favourite place by the hearth. {{peer}} suggests testing how long hospitality lasts.

outcome.text: {{carer}} makes room for both. The visitor tells a story worth more than the lost foot of warmth.

choices.label: Explain whose place it really is

outcome.text: {{carer}} hears the explanation and gives the visitor another blanket. {{peer}} suggests your case lacked witnesses.

title: THE SIGNATURE BIGGER THAN THE RENT
text: {{other}} asks you to witness a rent mark. The tenant cannot read; you can read just enough to see the amount has grown.

choices.label: Read the amount aloud before marking

outcome.text: {{other}} blames a tired clerk and fetches the smaller tally. The tenant watches you finish the word.

choices.label: Mark it and avoid the argument

outcome.text: {{other}} thanks you for being sensible. The tenant pays for the compliment.

title: THE MASTERPIECE SMALL ENOUGH TO HIDE
text: {{peer}} has made a model of the master’s best work and accidentally improved it. The master is approaching.

outcome.text: The master inspects the joint twice before asking how it was done. {{peer}} stops hiding the model beneath the bench.

choices.label: Present the model as your work

outcome.text: The master asks you to repeat the joint. {{peer}} watches your second, much less successful masterpiece.

title: THE ANSWER IN THE WRONG MARGIN
text: {{peer}} has a copy of a test with the answers written in the margin. The scholar’s name is also written there.

choices.label: Return the copy before the test

outcome.text: {{peer}} calls you unreasonable until the scholar starts collecting names as well as papers.
You reproduce the scholar’s name under your own. {{peer}} admires the completeness of your borrowing.

title: THE HEN HAS TWO OWNERS AND NO ALLEGIANCE
text: {{peer}} catches a hen claimed by two households. It lays an egg during the argument.

outcome.text: The mark settles ownership. {{peer}} asks whether the egg can remain neutral.

choices.label: Sell the egg while they debate

outcome.text: You gain one gold. {{peer}} has to explain why the hen has suddenly become less productive under joint ownership.

title: THE MESSAGE THAT SOUNDS BETTER SHORTENED
text: {{other}} entrusts you with a message that contains an apology. {{peer}} says removing that part would make you sound much more important.

outcome.text: {{other}} hears that you kept the difficult part. The reply is shorter because it no longer has to be angry.
Your version reaches the wrong sort of audience. {{other}} asks to hear the exact improvement, without the audience this time.

title: THE SWORD THAT REQUIRES TWO HANDS AND PERMISSION
text: {{peer}} finds a practice sword and suggests testing it before anyone can ask why you have it.

outcome.text: The instructor gives you a blunt exercise and a stance that does not involve the nearest wall. {{peer}} has to learn it too.
The sword strikes a bucket. {{peer}} concedes that the bucket has surrendered, though your wrist disputes the victory.

title: THE TRANSLATION THAT IMPROVES THE COOK
text: {{teacher}} assigns a Latin line. {{peer}} translates it as a command to give scholars better pudding.

outcome.text: The line concerns patience. {{teacher}} describes the translation as a practical opportunity to demonstrate it.
{{teacher}} asks for the grammatical reason. {{peer}} supplies an excellent account of hunger and no grammar.

title: THE EXTRA COIN NOBODY HAS CLAIMED
text: {{other}} gives you too much change. {{peer}} calculates how long it would take an honest person to notice.

outcome.text: {{other}} checks the sum and thanks you without making a sermon of it. {{peer}} revises the calculation.
You gain two gold. {{peer}} learns exactly which sort of mistake you prefer not to correct.

title: THE DARE WITH A WITNESS IN EVERY WINDOW
text: {{peer}} dares you over a forbidden fence. Every house overlooking it appears empty, except at the curtains.

outcome.text: {{peer}} calls you cautious. The curtains remain disappointed and your coat remains whole.

choices.label: Climb before the witnesses get comfortable

success.text: You cross and return with a leaf caught in your collar. {{peer}} declares the leaf proof of a great expedition.

failure.text: You tear your coat and scrape a knee. {{peer}} offers a version of events in which the fence attacked first.

title: THE NICKNAME THAT HAS OUTLIVED THE JOKE
text: {{peer}} gives you a name the younger children repeat without understanding. They are very diligent pupils.

choices.label: Ask plainly for it to stop

outcome.text: {{peer}} sees that you are not performing for the audience. The next attempt at the joke is quieter and much less certain.

choices.label: Invent a crueler name in return

outcome.text: The audience learns two names. {{peer}} begins collecting examples, and the game stops feeling like one.

title: THE HOUSEHOLD’S FIRST REAL ACCOUNT
text: {{carer}} lets you compare the household tally with the goods. The tally is much more optimistic.

outcome.text: {{carer}} changes the supper plan without blaming your arithmetic. The household has learned something useful before it becomes hungry.
{{carer}} finds the empty shelf. Your figures are moved to the category of things that require checking.

title: THE BRIDGE PLAN DRAWN AFTER THE RAIN
text: {{peer}} proposes building a footbridge from spare boards. The drawing includes a heroic figure in a cloak, but no supports.

outcome.text: {{peer}} removes the cloak to make room on the slate. The model now stands without needing anyone to be brave.

choices.label: Keep the heroic figure and test the model

outcome.text: The model folds beneath a pebble. {{peer}} moves the hero to the bank, where command appears much safer.

title: THE LETTER THAT HAS MET ITS READER
text: {{peer}} has read your carefully composed note and asks whether the excellent handwriting is meant to distract from the question.

choices.label: Ask honestly and accept the answer

outcome.text: You manage a conversation without borrowed verses. {{peer}} answers without inviting the lane to judge it.

choices.label: Claim you were copying an exercise

outcome.text: {{peer}} asks which lesson requires quite so many compliments about their eyes. The handwriting is admired at a distance.

title: THE WAGE WITH AN INVISIBLE DEDUCTION
text: {{other}} offers your first paid errand, less a fee for teaching you the privilege of being paid.

choices.label: Ask for the actual wage before agreeing

outcome.text: {{other}} removes the instructional fee after discovering you have understood that part without tuition.

choices.label: Accept the bad bargain for experience

outcome.text: You receive two gold and a lesson worth at least the missing two. {{other}} praises your cooperative nature.

title: THE BOOK THAT SHOULD NOT BE THIS INTERESTING
text: {{peer}} finds a forbidden page in a respectable book. The author has helpfully marked the exciting parts in red.

choices.label: Read it critically rather than circulate it

outcome.text: You identify the argument and its weaknesses. {{peer}} is disappointed to discover that scandal can require homework.

choices.label: Copy the red parts for everyone

outcome.text: The copies are traced by your distinctive red initials. {{peer}} suggests that anonymity might have required another colour.

title: THE SHORT WAY PAST THE QUARRY
text: {{peer}} knows a quicker path beneath loose quarry stone. The chief recommendation is that nobody responsible has approved it.

outcome.text: {{peer}} complains until you arrive with both ankles functioning. The longer story is much less impressive.

success.text: You cross safely and gain a poor example you can now defend from experience.

failure.text: Loose stone catches your leg. The broken bone ends the outing and begins a real recovery.

title: THE REFERENCE WRITTEN BY ITS BENEFICIARY
text: {{peer}} has written you a glowing reference for work. It praises three skills you do not yet possess and a fourth that nobody recognises.

choices.label: Correct the reference before using it

outcome.text: {{peer}} keeps one compliment you can defend. The employer receives a smaller promise and a more useful applicant.
The employer asks for a demonstration of the mysterious fourth skill. {{peer}} is suddenly unavailable to explain it.

title: THE BAG FOR THE LIFE BEYOND HOME
text: {{carer}} helps pack what you will need for work away from the household. Every practical object seems to carry a longer conversation.

choices.label: Pack slowly and hear the advice

outcome.text: {{carer}} stops pretending the extra bread is merely efficient. You leave the bag by the door and stay for the meal.

choices.label: Pack quickly to prove you are ready

outcome.text: {{carer}} adds the bread after you have finished explaining your independence. You notice it later.

title: THE SEED THAT IS ALSO SUPPER
text: {{carer}} divides the household’s seed grain. It looks uncomfortably like the food everyone could eat tonight.

choices.label: Keep the sowing reserve and find other work

outcome.text: {{carer}} marks the sack. The evening is lean, but the spring has not been eaten to make it easier.
The meal is better. {{carer}} counts the missing seed before putting the empty sack away.

title: THE SAMPLE BETTER THAN THE GOODS
text: {{carer}} shows you a perfect cloth sample and the less perfect consignment. The lesson is about which one customers are allowed to touch.

choices.label: Label the goods by what they are

outcome.text: The lower price earns fewer coins and fewer angry visits. {{carer}} lets you write the next honest description.

choices.label: Sell from the perfect sample alone

outcome.text: You receive four gold. {{carer}} makes you keep the sample for the complaints, where perfection becomes less helpful.

title: THE RATION RETURN COUNTS YOU TWICE
text: {{carer}} finds two ration entries in your name. The quartermaster describes the second as an administrative child.

outcome.text: The quartermaster crosses out the child. {{carer}} praises your first successful reduction of an army.
You gain food and lose the advantage of a simple explanation. {{carer}} puts both signatures beside you at supper.

title: THE CHAIR THAT OUTRANKS ITS OWNER
text: {{carer}} asks you to yield a chair to an important cousin. The cousin has brought a diagram establishing the chair’s ancestors.

choices.label: Move the chair and keep your wit private

outcome.text: {{carer}} sees the concession. The cousin spends supper defending the pedigree to a chair that cannot contradict it.

choices.label: Ask to hear the chair’s whole pedigree

outcome.text: The explanation lasts until the food cools. {{carer}} admires your question less than the audience does.

title: THE PRICE OF THE FIRE
text: {{other}} offers a healing stone for one fee and its warmth for another. The brazier is plainly visible.

outcome.text: You point to the brazier. {{other}} moves it behind a cloth, making the science harder to inspect.

choices.label: Show the customers how it is warmed

outcome.text: The customers warm their own stones. {{other}} has never disliked public education quite so much.

title: SILENCE AT THE MARKET RATE
text: Your rival {{other}} offers silence about a rumour. The offer is made loudly enough to demonstrate what the money would buy.

outcome.text: {{other}} raises the voice, then remembers everyone can now hear the price as well.
You repeat the offer exactly. {{other}} objects to the lack of discretion in your account of extortion.

title: THE ANCESTOR WITH TWO EXCLUSIVE FAMILIES
text: {{other}} offers an exclusive pedigree also displayed on a neighbouring stall. The ancestor appears to have reproduced chiefly through commissions.

outcome.text: {{other}} asks whether a smaller ancestor at a lower price might suit.
The clerk asks where you met the witness from 1180. {{other}} has stopped offering introductions.

charge.offence: Defending an invented pedigree under oath

title: THE MEASURE AT THE HEARING
text: {{other}} brings a milling measure to a dispute. Its outside is larger than its inside, a distinction the miller would prefer described less clearly.

choices.label: Describe only what you can inspect

outcome.text: The clerk records its capacity. {{other}} objects to a vessel being judged by what it holds.
The measure returns unchanged. {{other}} thanks you for an unusually spacious interpretation of silence.

title: QUILLS WITH AN HONEST PARENTAGE
text: {{other}} sells ordinary quills with a plain description. The prices are the only part claiming celestial distinction.

outcome.text: {{other}} sells a bird’s feather as a bird’s feather. Nobody is asked to kneel.
The buyers laugh and {{other}} closes the box. Accuracy has become personal rather than profitable.

title: THE INFORMANT’S WELL-KEPT COPY
text: You have a known secret. {{other}} offers to suppress a political accusation already circulating in the market. The offer is the fresh part.

outcome.text: You state your position publicly. {{other}} discovers that information loses value when its owner can say it aloud.

choices.label: Buy one copy, without trusting it is unique (12g)

outcome.text: {{other}} promises exactly one sheet, which is the most honest part of the interview.

title: THE MIRACLE’S EXPENSE ACCOUNT
text: {{other}} asks whether shrine donations should buy food or a larger sign describing the shrine’s generosity.

outcome.text: The money becomes bread. {{other}} agrees the sign would have been harder to divide between households.
{{other}} opens the empty bread basket beside the full account. The distinction needs no Latin.

title: THE LUNCH COLLECTOR HAS LOST THE BADGE
text: {{other}} collects lunches for the older children. The badge is a leaf, and the older children deny employing a leaf.

outcome.text: {{other}} drops the badge. You leave the lunches where their owners can reach them.
{{other}} recognises the method. You have abolished the collector by taking the job.

title: THE CARE THAT IS NOT AN INVOICE
text: Your mother {{other}} asks whether accepting help means hearing the cost repeated at every meal.

choices.label: Say care is not a debt between you

outcome.text: {{other}} puts away the tally. You talk about the meal while it is warm.

choices.label: Explain every sacrifice you have made

outcome.text: The tally stays on the table. Repetition has not made the sum kinder.

title: THE GRIEVANCE WITHOUT THE GLOVE
text: Roderick arrives to state a grievance in words. {{other}} has left the glove at home and regards this as a considerable concession.

outcome.text: Roderick finishes without applause or a weapon. The grievance shrinks when nobody is performing it.
Roderick produces the glove after all. It was in the other pocket, with several less patient sentences.

title: THE LIVING PERSON ON THE DEAD LIST
text: {{other}} finds their name on a death assessment and asks whether correcting it will also restore the ordinary taxes.

outcome.text: {{other}} accepts that being alive is an expensive legal position, but preferable to the alternative.
{{other}} insists the receipt mention that the payer is still breathing.

title: THE FEE FOR NOT HAVING DIED
text: {{other}} offers to withdraw a doubtful death claim and charge for storing it. The dead are apparently expected to rent parchment.

outcome.text: {{other}} calls this unprecedented, then puts the form in a box full of precedents.
{{other}} starts searching for a clerk young enough to blame for inventing it.

title: THE HOUSEHOLD’S EMERGENCY RESERVE
text: {{other}} weighs the reserve before hiding it beneath the salt. The weighing is partly arithmetic and partly a question about trust.

outcome.text: Your contribution goes under the salt. {{other}} gives you the box instead of watching your hands.
You count openly. {{other}} stops treating the lid as something that needs a guard.

title: THE SIGNATURE YOU DID NOT WRITE
text: {{other}} has put your name beneath a loan guarantee. It is a handsome signature for a hand you do not recognise.

outcome.text: The lender asks {{other}} for their own security. The sudden interest in spelling is unwelcome.
You pay and cross out the supposed signature. {{other}} thanks you more quietly than the money deserves.

title: THE CHILD WHO SAW THE HIDDEN GOODS
text: Your child {{other}} has found goods hidden from a collector and asks how old a person must be before lying becomes lawful.

outcome.text: You explain the wrong rather than the advantage. {{other}} asks another question; the first answer mattered.
{{other}} stops asking. This is much less reassuring than you expected.

title: THE FAMILY SEAL SMELLS OF SOAP
text: {{other}} has cut a family seal in soap. The impression is convincing; the basin is full of evidence.

outcome.text: The document is corrected and the soap used for washing. {{other}} finds both applications disappointing.

choices.label: Use the impression on another paper

outcome.text: The clerk recognises the same bubbles on both. {{other}} has made a very washable conspiracy.

charge.offence: Creating false evidence for the soap-seal advance

title: TWO PEOPLE, ONE HOUSEHOLD LIST
text: {{other}} wants the household goods counted fairly. The difficult contributions have never fitted on a list.

outcome.text: {{other}} stops adding the small corrections designed merely to make you listen.

choices.label: Claim every advantage on the list

outcome.text: You keep the better goods. {{other}} keeps a copy that now resembles a description of you.

title: THE JOKE YOUR SPOUSE DID NOT ENJOY
text: {{other}} asks about your public joke concerning the marriage. The audience has gone, taking most of its persuasive force.

outcome.text: {{other}} accepts before you can improve the apology into another performance.
{{other}} asks whether you intend to live with everybody else.

title: THE UNCOUNTED WEDDING EXPENSE
text: {{other}} brings a wedding bill for an extra musician, borrowed benches and a creditor nobody invited.

outcome.text: {{other}} dismisses the extra musician, who had been charging to wait.
The feast shrinks. The creditor is the only guest pleased to see a smaller table.

title: THE SINGER AND THE NUMBERED WINDOWS
text: {{other}} has hired a serenade below the wrong window. The actual listener is pricing an encore.

outcome.text: The singer moves a window along. Only one household has learned the entire verse.
The street joins the refrain. {{other}} hears their own name more clearly than the lover’s.

title: THE RENT ON YOUR OWN SHADE
text: Your feuding households disagree again. {{other}} claims rent for a wall’s shade, making the afternoon unusually expensive.

outcome.text: {{other}} hears a concession rather than a threat. The feud remains, but this conversation has not enlarged it.
The crowd laughs. {{other}} adds the audience to an account that was already long enough.

title: THE PARDON HAS LEFT ROOM FOR EVERYONE
text: You face legal suspicion. {{other}} offers a pardon with the offence left blank: an unusually broad mercy in an unsworn hand.

outcome.text: {{other}} offers a smaller offence at a lower price. The paper becomes less forgiving by the word.

choices.label: Show the blank to the clerk

outcome.text: The clerk fills the space with an inquiry into {{other}}. It is the first named matter the paper has covered.

title: THE PIE COMES WITH INSTRUCTIONS
text: {{other}} offers you a pie to deliver to a juror. The note inside the crust has not been written by a cook.

outcome.text: {{other}} removes the note and asks about the pie alone. Its innocence has survived less well than its pastry.
{{other}} gets the pie back without the private understanding it was meant to contain.

title: THE PRICE OFFERED FOR YOUR SKIN
text: {{other}} offers money if you take somebody else’s punishment. The payment is specified more carefully than the scar.

outcome.text: The crowd hears the price. {{other}} discovers how cheaply an offer becomes a public description.
{{other}} explains it without accountancy. The bargain sounds considerably worse.

title: THE COFFIN NEEDS ANOTHER RECEIPT
text: {{other}} demands a toll from a funeral cart. The deceased must establish residence before being permitted to leave it.

outcome.text: {{other}} finds no rate for the particular journey being proposed.
{{other}} supplies a receipt that would embarrass any living person asked to present it.

title: THE OATH REHEARSED TOO WELL
text: {{other}} wants you to repeat a polished account before a clerk. Your current legal difficulties make the friendship unusually attentive.

outcome.text: {{other}} folds the script and asks whether you have always been so difficult to assist.
The clerk receives a script instead of an oath. {{other}} did not expect to be its main character.

title: THE BARREL HAS MOSTLY CARRIED AIR
text: {{other}} disputes a delivery with an excellent barrel mark and little inside. The mark cannot be poured into a cup.

outcome.text: {{other}} signs for what arrived and stops praising the beauty of the cooperage.
{{other}} keeps the barrel as an exhibit. It is lighter than your explanation.

title: THE CUSTOMER KEPT THE BROKEN PART
text: {{other}} brings defective work and its receipt. The receipt has aged better than the joint.

choices.label: Replace the fault at your expense (10g)

outcome.text: {{other}} keeps the new receipt without requiring an apology to hold the work together.
{{other}} places the broken joint beside the untouched one. The comparison is shorter than your defence.

title: THE CREDITOR HAS NEVER BEEN TO SEA
text: You owe money. {{other}} explains that water damage is a matter between you and the goods.

choices.label: Review the terms without promising payment

outcome.text: {{other}} reads the terms with you. The loan remains a debt, but neither of you can now describe it differently.
The debt acquires a younger sibling. {{other}} has recorded the new promise as carefully as the first.

title: THE SILENT PARTNER HAS A SPEECH
text: {{other}} proposes a partnership. “Silent” appears to be a title rather than a restriction on giving orders.

choices.label: Agree clear limits before taking money

outcome.text: {{other}} reads the terms twice. Silence has become specific enough to price.
{{other}} delivers the remaining speech to someone who has not already declined it.

title: THE WORD THAT CHANGES THE TESTIMONY
text: {{other}} presents a copied statement missing “not”. The clerk calls it a small word, as though size settled its effect.

outcome.text: The clerk inserts “not” and discovers that the sentence has become more expensive to defend.
{{other}} has kept a second copy. Your attempt to improve the evidence has become part of it.

charge.offence: Destroying evidence of a deliberately altered agreement

title: THE CERTIFICATE’S INCONVENIENT DATE
text: {{other}} queries a medical certificate dated when you were not present. Your profession makes the date more important than the handwriting.

outcome.text: {{other}} accepts the correction and keeps the original. It records what you signed, not what you wish to have meant.
{{other}} produces the dated envelope. Your memory has developed a very difficult relationship with the post.

title: THE PATRON’S ALMOST HARMLESS VERSE
text: {{other}} commissions a poem naming no victim until the last line. That line is underlined twice.

choices.label: Keep the point and remove the target

outcome.text: {{other}} complains that everybody could learn from it. You agree to regard this as a defect.
{{other}} takes the underlined line to a poet with fewer objections and more hunger.

title: THE MEN WHO FIT THE MUSTER
text: {{other}} brings a muster smaller than the proposed parade. The flags have been ordered for the larger version.

outcome.text: The spare flags become the only part of the company without duties. {{other}} signs the honest return.
The company laughs. {{other}} must defend honesty and the size of the banners at once.

title: THE DINNER QUARREL BETWEEN TWO HOUSES
text: Your families maintain a feud. {{other}} brings a disputed dining account and a fresh opportunity to explain your relations.

outcome.text: {{other}} hears an admission rather than an inherited speech. The feud remains, but this meeting has not added to it.
{{other}} writes it down exactly. Both houses now possess another version they will prefer not to correct.

title: THE RIVER REFUSES THE DRAWING
text: {{other}} maps the river on the profitable side of a boundary. The river is available outside for comparison.

outcome.text: {{other}} puts the river where it is. The survey keeps enough dignity to be useful.

choices.label: Explain the first drawing’s advantages publicly

outcome.text: The audience laughs. {{other}} wishes the river had been less cooperative with the joke.

title: THE FACE IS SOUND, THE SILVER IS LIGHT
text: {{other}} brings coins bearing your royal face and less silver than required. The portrait has suffered no corresponding reduction.

outcome.text: {{other}} leaves with a written standard rather than another promise about your nose.

choices.label: Blame the people weighing the coins

outcome.text: {{other}} weighs another. The missing silver continues to be absent without asking permission.

title: THE VERDICT ARRIVES BEFORE THE WITNESSES
text: {{other}} brings the ruler a petition with its conclusion already written. The witnesses have been invited to agree.

outcome.text: {{other}} removes the conclusion from the top. The witnesses acquire a purpose they were not promised.
The petition leaves by the public door. {{other}} has failed to purchase the convenience of your name.

title: THE SAINT HAS TWO CHILDHOODS
text: {{other}} displays two skulls of one saint, one adult and one child. The smaller is offered at a family price.

outcome.text: One skull loses a childhood and gains a description {{other}} can defend.

choices.label: Tell the crowd the original explanation

outcome.text: The crowd asks for the saint’s youth at a middling price. {{other}} closes the case.

title: THE OVEN’S EVIDENCE IS ON YOUR HAND
text: You live with chronic pain. {{other}} recommends an ordeal by heat, having found no other method of making your day more convincing.

choices.label: Explain what pain does not prove

outcome.text: {{other}} must explain why your existing pain has failed to supply sufficient evidence.
{{other}} brings a chair and stops discussing the oven. The day eases; the disability remains.

title: THE DONORS SPEAK BEFORE THE BREAD
text: {{other}} organises relief. Donors demand their names be read before the recipients eat.

choices.label: Serve food while reading the names

outcome.text: {{other}} reads over grateful chewing. The list finally provides a useful accompaniment.

choices.label: Make the hungry wait for important names

outcome.text: The list is magnificent. {{other}} looks at the cooling food and stops admiring its length.

title: THE BANDAGE AND THE SMALL REQUEST
text: You have a wound under care. {{other}} helps with the dressing and asks for practical help when you are able.

choices.label: Offer help you can safely give

outcome.text: {{other}} accepts a useful promise instead of an impossible display of gratitude.
{{other}} finishes carefully. The knot receives more attention than the conversation.

title: THE SMALLEST PART OF THE SCAFFOLD
text: {{other}} calls a loose scaffold peg too small to matter. Everybody is preparing to stand above it.

outcome.text: {{other}} watches the platform stop moving and lowers the peg’s size on the list of objections.

choices.label: Explain mostly your own good sense

outcome.text: {{other}} fits the peg while you conclude. One contribution makes the scaffold safer.

title: THE GUARANTEE FITS IN THE BOTTLE
text: {{other}} offers a guarantee promising only that the bottle contains tonic. The lettering is much smaller than “guarantee”.

outcome.text: {{other}} lists ingredients without offering to rearrange your future. The smaller promise is refreshing.
{{other}} accepts that an honest label does not create a thirsty customer.

title: THE FORTUNE CHARGES IN ADVANCE
text: You already owe money. {{other}} offers a foreign fortune whose estate is unnamed and whose fees are well documented.

outcome.text: {{other}} produces another seal. You retain the advantage of owing nothing to it.

choices.label: Take the demands to the clerk

outcome.text: The clerk asks for the estate’s name before its next fee. {{other}} dislikes this new order of business.

title: THE DEVIL WANTS AN HONEST WAGE
text: {{other}} accounts for a pageant whose devil has worked more than the angels and received less than the donkey.

outcome.text: The devil is paid. {{other}} ends an infernal dispute without theology.
The devil thanks you for not explaining that art should be its own reward.

title: THE BOUNDARY STONE HAS AN AUDIENCE
text: {{other}} asks where a family boundary belongs. The witnesses remember its position, unless somebody first suggests an advantage.

outcome.text: {{other}} helps put the stone back before bargaining can improve everyone’s memory.
{{other}} seeks another witness. The stone remains less evasive than its neighbours.

title: THE KEEPSAKE WITHOUT A NEW PRICE
text: {{other}} gives you a family keepsake. This one, the explanation goes, should not need another household account.

choices.label: Accept without making a debt of the gift

outcome.text: You listen to its story. {{other}} stops waiting for you to price the kindness.

choices.label: List what your help has cost

outcome.text: {{other}} sets the keepsake beside the tally. The two objects make an unkind comparison.

title: THE VICTORY BOW BEFORE THE RACE
text: {{other}} has challenged you before witnesses, drawn the finish line and rehearsed a victory bow. The race has not yet acquired a second willing participant.

success.text: You finish first. {{other}} delivers the rehearsed bow to entirely the wrong audience.

failure.text: You finish behind {{other}}, but well ahead of the sack you were supposed to carry. The crowd generously counts this as two competitions.

choices.label: Make the rules public before agreeing

outcome.text: The witnesses reject three of {{other}}’s rules and the foot planted on your starting line. The contest is abandoned on grounds of sudden fatigue.
{{other}} objects to being pitied, then accepts the other handle. Neither of you wins; the intended owner finally receives the sack.

title: THE BUSHEL WITH A SECOND PRICE
text: The harvest is poor. {{other}} has raised the price of grain while the parish is still thanking God for having any. The poor box is being asked to pay retail.

outcome.text: You put grain in the household reserve and invite neighbours to draw against a written tally. {{other}} asks whether generosity has to be so well organised.

choices.label: Sell your stored grain at the new price

outcome.text: Your purse fills as the household shelves empty. {{other}} congratulates you in a voice intended to carry to the queue.

choices.label: Check the merchant’s measure in public

outcome.text: The scoop has an excellent appetite. You demonstrate it before the buyers; {{other}} produces a fuller measure and a considerably shorter greeting.

title: THE WILL WITH ROOM FOR ANOTHER SIGNATURE
text: {{other}} claims the household inheritance. The witness has helpfully left a blank beside the signature, in case the dead should wish to improve the arrangement.

outcome.text: The witnessed inventory puts the disputed goods beyond {{other}}’s reach. The clerk charges for the copy and, after a pause, for the original being correct.
You surrender part of the goods and end the claim in writing. {{other}} accepts, having discovered that a smaller inheritance weighs less than another argument.
Your version is wonderfully clear and legally disastrous. {{other}} recognises the ink, and the clerk finally has a document worth investigating.
The goods leave with {{other}}. You close the door on the argument and stand for a while where the better chest used to be.

title: THE CART THAT HAS ALREADY ENLISTED
text: {{other}} brings a levy writ for men, grain and carts. Your cart is listed as willing. The horse has expressed no view that the clerk is prepared to record.

choices.label: Pay for supplies in place of bodies (18g)

outcome.text: The official accepts supplies against your household’s obligation. The horse remains a civilian and looks deeply ungrateful.
You insist on a public list and exemptions read aloud. {{other}} objects to giving the levy quite so many opportunities to understand it.

choices.label: List a dead man in your household’s place

outcome.text: The dead man is exceptionally punctual on paper. His burial entry is equally punctual in reaching the clerk.

title: THE FUTURE THAT DOES NOT FIT THE HOUSE
text: {{child}} has a plan larger than the household can afford. The explanation includes a drawing of the future workshop and a very small space labelled “parents”.

outcome.text: You pay for tools and instruction. {{child}} redraws the parents’ space with a window.

choices.label: Help test the idea before promising money

outcome.text: You work through the first task together. {{child}} finds three problems and a fourth reason to keep trying.

choices.label: Order the child to take your place instead

outcome.text: {{child}} folds the drawing carefully and stops showing you the revisions. The household has gained obedience at the price of confidence.

title: THE LORD’S THREE DRIEST DAYS
text: {{other}} calls boon-work on the only dry days available for your hay. The notice describes this as a fortunate coincidence.

outcome.text: You divide the service and harvest between households. Everybody complains about the rota, which has the unusual advantage of leaving time to complain.
The steward accepts eight gold and stops praising the spiritual value of labour. Your hay is gathered before the rain.

choices.label: Take a neighbour’s paid work instead

outcome.text: You earn the wage while your own stores suffer. {{other}} records your absence with rather more enthusiasm than your presence ever received.

title: THE PRICE CHANGED WHILE YOU WERE WORKING
text: {{other}} brings the new assize price just as your goods are ready. It has moved down. The cost of making them has displayed less religious humility.

choices.label: Correct the price and publish the weights

outcome.text: You accept the smaller margin. The wardens inspect your measure twice, disappointed to find nothing worth carrying away.

choices.label: Keep the old price and shorten the measure

outcome.text: The first buyers pay well. {{other}} brings the scoop to the wardens; your profit now has to attend a hearing.

charge.offence: Selling with a shortened assize measure

choices.label: Sell honestly at a loss to keep the customers

outcome.text: You swallow the loss before anyone has to swallow your explanation. {{other}} recommends the shop without being paid to do it.

title: THE CHILD BEFORE THE PEDIGREE
text: {{other}} brings a weak newborn to the chapel. Someone asks about the mother’s marriage. The child is having difficulty waiting for the answer.

choices.label: Attend to the child before the argument

outcome.text: You arrange warmth and immediate care. {{other}} thanks you; the questioner is left holding a pedigree nobody presently needs.
The midwife enters, sends the debaters outside and asks for clean cloth. The room becomes much more useful.

choices.label: Insist the household settle the paperwork first

outcome.text: {{other}} leaves to find help elsewhere. The forms remain beautifully arranged on a table that is suddenly too quiet.

title: SIX ARCHERS SHORT OF AN ARMY
text: {{other}} needs six archers before the muster ends. One volunteer can draw a bow; the other five can draw their names with assistance.

choices.label: Train the volunteers and report their limits

outcome.text: You submit an honest muster and a useful drill. {{other}} has fewer imaginary archers and more actual ones.

choices.label: Supply six magnificent names on paper

outcome.text: The company pays for six archers who have achieved complete concealment. The muster clerk takes an interest in your handwriting.

choices.label: Pay a veteran to run the drill (8g)

outcome.text: The veteran teaches the company to hit the target and you to stop standing beside it.

title: THE CHARGE NOBODY HAS READ
text: {{other}} presents fourteen charges against tenants, four of whom cannot read them. The proposed procedure is to ask whether they understand and fine them for saying no.

choices.label: Read every charge and hear the answers

outcome.text: The hearing takes all afternoon. Two charges collapse, three improve dramatically when spoken aloud, and your tenants discover a use for your chair.

choices.label: Collect the proposed fines without a hearing

outcome.text: Your household gains twenty gold. The tenants learn that silence is the cheapest answer, and {{other}} begins bringing shorter rolls with larger totals.
The new clerk finds a hen charged twice and a man fined for being the hen’s owner. {{other}} disputes the hen’s legal personality.

title: THE ELEVENTH ITEM IS THE COINAGE
text: {{other}} places the currency proposal eleventh on a twenty-item agenda. The first ten concern ceremonial cushions. By the eleventh, the council will agree to almost any metal.

outcome.text: The mint keeps its standard and the cushions endure neglect. {{other}} discovers that rearranging business can be a form of government.

choices.label: Sell exemptions before discussing the standard

outcome.text: Twenty gold reaches your purse. The exemptions reach the clerk’s book, where they are much less easily spent.
The assayer demonstrates the difference between the portrait and the silver. Nobody applauds until they know which one you meant to protect.

title: THE BAND’S LIST OF THINGS NOT TO STEAL
text: {{other}} proposes a rule against robbing poor households. The band asks how poor, how often, and whether the rule applies before supper.

choices.label: Keep the rule and divide your own supplies

outcome.text: You give up food and keep the band’s trust. {{other}} adds “including when hungry” in lettering large enough for everyone.

choices.label: Limit the plan to a wealthy target

outcome.text: The proposal acquires a richer victim and a proper robbery charge. {{other}} approves of your principles being so profitable.
The authorities pay twelve gold. {{other}} learns which part of the agreement you considered negotiable.

title: THE DEBT DISCUSSED IN A DOORWAY
text: {{other}} asks you to guarantee a loan. The request is made quietly in a doorway, as though a witness might add to the interest.

choices.label: Lend from your own purse instead (8g)

outcome.text: You put your own coins on the table and set down the terms. {{other}} accepts the help without having to borrow your name as well.
The loan is entered in your name. {{other}} promises gratitude; the lender prefers your signature.

choices.label: Refuse kindly and keep the friendship separate

outcome.text: {{other}} goes quiet, then asks whether you can help carry the goods instead. The friendship has survived acquiring a boundary.

title: HALF A FURROW, ALL OF YOUR ENEMITY
text: {{other}} has moved the boundary by half a furrow. The argument is now occupying more ground than the disputed field.

outcome.text: The survey proves both of you wrong by a little. {{other}} dislikes this result almost as much as losing.

choices.label: Trade the strip for an end to the personal quarrel

outcome.text: You give up a small claim. {{other}} takes your hand before either of you can turn it into another condition.
Your household gains from the disputed use. {{other}} brings witnesses to the new fence, which has failed to make itself invisible.

title: THE SILENCE HAS JOINED YOU FOR SUPPER
text: {{spouse}} sets out two bowls and a list of household decisions made without consultation. The list needs more table than the bowls.

choices.label: Agree new terms and hear the whole list

outcome.text: You share the household accounts and the work. {{spouse}} finally eats before the soup becomes another grievance.
You end the marriage by consent. The practical divisions are written down; neither of you tries to make the last conversation a victory.

choices.label: Insist the matter is already settled

outcome.text: {{spouse}} folds the list and stops discussing it. The quiet you wanted has become much less comfortable.

title: SEVEN NIGHTS YOU DID NOT SIT UP
text: {{sibling}} cared for your parent through the last illness. You were away. The account between you is not mainly about money, but money is the easiest part to say.

choices.label: Acknowledge the burden without an excuse

outcome.text: You say what you should have said before discussing the household goods. {{sibling}} sits down. The practical argument can finally begin.
You put ten gold toward the household costs. {{sibling}} accepts it without agreeing that the amount explains the nights.

choices.label: Describe the care as a duty owed anyway

outcome.text: {{sibling}} says that is an interesting use of the word “owed”. The household division becomes colder and much more exact.

title: THE LIFE YOU HAD ALREADY ARRANGED
text: {{child}} tells you the planned apprenticeship is not the life they want. The master is waiting outside with an agreement that leaves very little room for wanting.

outcome.text: You return the unsigned agreement and work through a different first step. {{child}} explains it twice, because this time you are listening.

choices.label: Pay for a short trial in the chosen work (8g)

outcome.text: You buy a trial rather than a future. {{child}} thanks you for the distinction and immediately starts asking practical questions.
The paper remains unsigned while you argue. {{child}} learns exactly how much confidence to place in the next invitation to speak freely.

title: THREE SMALL THINGS AND A VERY LARGE QUESTION
text: You have three small reasons to distrust {{spouse}}. Each would be nothing on its own. You can ask a question, or spend a great deal of effort turning them into a verdict.

outcome.text: {{spouse}} answers and shows you the disputed letter. You discuss the real quarrel instead of the imaginary witness you were about to invent.
The inquiry produces receipts, gossip and a bill. It produces no proof. {{spouse}} discovers the bill first.

choices.label: End a marriage you no longer trust

outcome.text: You agree to separate. The uncertainty remains uncertainty; neither of you puts an unproved accusation into the record.

title: THE ROAD BY THE FEVER HOUSES
text: {{other}} reports sickness beside the ford. The traders want the road kept open, preferably with the sick encouraged to describe it more quietly.

choices.label: Fund separate supplies and a temporary cordon (12g)

outcome.text: You send food to the affected houses and keep the gathering apart. {{other}} has to explain to the traders that a queue can carry more than baskets.

choices.label: Sell a reassuring account to the traders

outcome.text: The traders pay for an open road and a closed mouth. The parish’s sickness burden rises; {{other}} knows who supplied the reassurance.

choices.label: Organise bearers and food without inventing a cure

outcome.text: You spend your strength on practical care. {{other}} works beside you; neither of you wastes the breath on promises.

title: THE MARKET THAT FORGOT TO BE LAWFUL
text: Swineford has held a market for years without a charter. {{other}} brings a rival town’s complaint and a lawyer who has already found the fee schedule.

outcome.text: The petition is lodged with the market’s accounts and your payment. {{other}} signs beside you; the lawyer has to find an actual objection.
The wax is old. The clerk recognises a witness who has been alive for only nineteen years, and takes a much livelier interest.
Both towns accept a smaller return and stop paying lawyers to describe the same stalls. {{other}} calls this a regrettable outbreak of arithmetic.

title: TWO GREAT SEALS, ONE TAX DEMAND
text: {{other}} presents two contradictory orders bearing rival seals. Both demand the same money. The messengers insist that obedience is a simple matter.

choices.label: Publish both orders and refuse duplicate payment

outcome.text: You pay the recorded obligation once and keep witnessed copies. {{other}} has to explain why loyalty should require a second receipt.

choices.label: Sell your support to the richer messenger

outcome.text: You accept fifteen gold for an endorsement. The rival claimant keeps the copy with your name; {{other}} keeps the original.
The verifier identifies the duplicate demand. One messenger objects to being described as a man with a very expensive stamp.

title: THE ACCUSATION ALREADY IN INK
text: {{other}} has entered a small accusation against you with magnificent certainty. The evidence consists of having heard it from someone who was also certain.

outcome.text: The witnesses disagree about the day, the place and your hat. {{other}} withdraws the accusation in defence of the one detail they still like.

choices.label: Pay to settle the civil claim (8g)

outcome.text: The disputed claim is withdrawn with a receipt. {{other}} is pleased with your reasonableness, which appears to have been priced exactly.
The alibi improves until the clerk asks for a date. You have supplied a real perjury charge in place of a doubtful accusation.

title: THIRTEEN DOORS, FOUR PAIRS OF HANDS
text: {{other}} has thirteen households asking for care and help for four. The richest house has sent a servant to explain how urgently wealth can suffer.

choices.label: Prioritise need and publish the list

outcome.text: The four places go to the most urgent cases. {{other}} helps explain the list to people who had hoped an explanation could be bought.
You pay for clean cloth, fuel and another pair of hands. {{other}} crosses two names off the waiting list before thanking you.

choices.label: Give priority to those who can pay you

outcome.text: You collect the fees. {{other}} has to deliver the refusal to the other doors and does not forgive the errand.

title: THE HOUSEHOLD THAT FITS IN THE YARD
text: Your family is safe outside a damaged home. {{other}} offers rebuilding credit while the timbers are still warm enough to make the interest seem reasonable.

outcome.text: The loan is recorded and the work is paid for. You get a weatherproof room and a creditor whose memory is much better than the thatch.
You save the usable timber and accept less space. {{other}} lends a hand after discovering that you intend to sleep under this work yourself.
You pay, count the spars and decline the loan. {{other}} looks disappointed by a roof that will not send them money.

title: THE NAVE HAS ACQUIRED A BORDER
text: Two priests have divided the parish over obedience and poverty. {{other}} asks where you sit. The draughtiest pew is now a declaration of belief.

choices.label: Make both sides state the practical complaint

outcome.text: The argument shrinks to a disputed charge for candles. {{other}} produces the account; the nave loses a frontier and gains an embarrassing sum.

choices.label: Sell a useful account to the richer side

outcome.text: You receive twelve gold and provide the quarrel with respectable language. {{other}} recognises the price even where the parish cannot read it.

choices.label: Fund parish food instead of another sermon (8g)

outcome.text: The food crosses the aisle without difficulty. {{other}} admits that hunger has been a rather efficient ecumenist.

title: THE CELLAR WITH A CANDIDATE ATTACHED
text: {{other}} seeks your vote against a rival with better wine. The election has reached the stage at which principles are being judged by the jug.

outcome.text: The voters must supply names rather than noises from the cellar. {{other}} accepts the result and blames the handwriting only once.

choices.label: Sell your vote and keep the cup

outcome.text: You receive ten gold. {{other}} keeps an exact account of the principle you sold and the much smaller cup you stole.

choices.label: Put forward an honest working candidate

outcome.text: You argue for skill rather than the cellar. {{other}} respects the argument while becoming much less fond of its author.

title: THE PRIORY’S NAMELESS PAYMENT
text: {{other}} brings a priory account for a child’s keep. The donor’s name is hidden; the expense is not. Someone has paid a great deal to be described as nobody.

choices.label: Pay the child’s immediate board without claiming a pedigree (12g)

outcome.text: The priory takes the money and serves supper. {{other}} puts away the royal speculation long enough to count the bowls.

choices.label: Publish the account as evidence, not proof of parentage

outcome.text: The payment becomes public. {{other}} finds that the missing name attracts more attention than any name you could safely invent.

choices.label: Accept payment to hide the account

outcome.text: You pocket fifteen gold and keep a secret. The unknown donor remains unknown; {{other}} is now quite certain about you.

title: FIFTEEN MISSING HOLY OBJECTS
text: {{other}} has an abbey inventory naming fifteen lost treasures. Four are on display in other churches. One is being used to keep a door open.

choices.label: Record where the objects actually are

outcome.text: You copy the marks and locations. {{other}} rescues the doorstop’s description before anyone can improve its provenance.

choices.label: Pay to return the disputed object (10g)

outcome.text: The abbey receives its object and the parish receives an ordinary stone for the door. Both are asked to acknowledge the substitution in writing.

choices.label: Sell the object to a discreet collector

outcome.text: You collect eighteen gold. The inventory becomes the evidence against you, with unusually helpful illustrations.

title: THE FRATERNITY’S LOCKED POOR BOX
text: {{other}} invites you to a fraternity that feeds its sick and buries its dead. The accounts are sound; the door is locked; the treasurer would prefer not to discuss the combination.

choices.label: Pay this year’s dues after reading the accounts (8g)

outcome.text: The fraternity records your contribution and opens the relief box. {{other}} welcomes the only new member who asked to see the bottom of it.

choices.label: Challenge the missing relief money publicly

outcome.text: The missing sum is entered beside the treasurer’s name. {{other}} loses your confidence and gains an audience for the explanation.

choices.label: Take a share for keeping quiet

outcome.text: You receive twelve gold from a box meant for sick neighbours. {{other}} considers this admission sufficiently binding without an oath.

title: THE MATCH WITH FOUR COPIES AND NO AGREEMENT
text: {{other}} brings a marriage settlement that promises more than either household owns. The clerk recommends signing before anyone counts.

outcome.text: The promised ox becomes a cart, then half a cart, then an apology. {{other}} agrees to a smaller honest settlement; nobody is married by arithmetic alone.
The proposed match ends before anybody has to live inside it. {{other}} returns your token with the air of a creditor cancelling a very small kingdom.
The settlement now contains enough cattle to feed both families until the clerk asks where they are. {{other}} supplies the false document to the court.

title: THE CHILD AT THE THRESHOLD
text: {{other}} brings a child needing a home. The parish offers a blessing and asks whether you can provide the less portable necessities.

choices.label: Register a placement and set aside food

outcome.text: The placement is entered through the parish and food is reserved. {{other}} carries away a practical answer instead of another prayer to translate into supper.
The parish receives eight gold for food and bedding. {{other}} puts the blessing aside long enough to buy both.

choices.label: Admit that your household cannot provide care

outcome.text: You help {{other}} ask elsewhere without promising a bed you do not have. The answer hurts less than a welcome that cannot be kept.

title: THE BED THAT HAS BECOME A PEDIGREE
text: {{sibling}} claims the best bed as the elder child. The argument has acquired three ancestors, two doubtful customs and no spare mattress.

outcome.text: You accept fewer goods in exchange for a final settlement. {{sibling}} signs before an ancestor can be found who slept on the floor.

choices.label: Give the bed and keep the relationship

outcome.text: {{sibling}} sits on the bed and, after an awkward pause, asks you to stay for supper.

choices.label: Produce a more convenient family inventory

outcome.text: The inventory is convincing until {{sibling}} remembers carving the listed chest last winter. A forgery complaint replaces the question of blankets.

title: THE MILLRACE’S BAD AIR
text: {{other}} has fever after clearing the millrace. The miller insists the work cannot be responsible because it was not paid well enough to be important.

outcome.text: You pay for food, water and a dry place to rest. {{other}} is spared the miller’s proposed cure of another shift.
You clear enough of the race to stop the immediate flooding. {{other}} thanks you; your own strength pays the part the miller omitted.

choices.label: Sell a reassuring report to keep the mill open

outcome.text: The miller pays you to call it a rumour. {{other}} supplies a less convenient account, between bouts of coughing.

title: THE MIDWIFE’S INCONVENIENT HAND
text: {{other}} is helping an experienced midwife whose hand locks in the cold. A family wants the famous name; the apprentice has the steadier fingers.

outcome.text: The midwife directs and the apprentice works. {{other}} marvels that two people can be useful without one of them being declared a fraud.

choices.label: Ask the midwife to choose the safest arrangement

outcome.text: The master gives the practical tasks to the apprentice and keeps the difficult decisions. {{other}} finally stops arguing about the name on the door.

choices.label: Insist on the name you were promised

outcome.text: The midwife attempts too much and the care becomes less safe. {{other}} remembers your contribution to a problem you did not have to solve with your hands.

title: THE BELL FOUNDER CANNOT READ HIS MARK
text: {{other}} cannot see the tuning marks on a new bell. The wardens want the famous founder to work alone, preferably without describing what “alone” now requires.

choices.label: Read the marks without taking the credit

outcome.text: You call the marks and {{other}} makes the corrections. The bell rings true, under the name that knew what to do with the numbers.

choices.label: Take the credit for the whole casting

outcome.text: You collect a fee and the applause. {{other}} keeps the mould and the knowledge of who actually knew how to use it.

choices.label: Pay for an assistant named on the commission (10g)

outcome.text: The wardens allow a second name after discovering it does not make the bell twice as expensive. {{other}} can keep working without pretending to see.

title: THE CHALICE AND THE VERY ORDINARY METAL
text: A chalice is missing. {{other}} has found a gilt shaving, a fresh roof and several hens belonging to a suspiciously prosperous witness.

choices.label: Have the metal tested before accusing anyone (5g)

outcome.text: The gold is gilt over pewter. {{other}} looks at the new roof and realises that someone has stolen twice: first the chalice, then the parish’s idea of its value.

choices.label: Place the evidence before the proper court

outcome.text: You lodge the shaving and the account of the payment. {{other}} signs as witness; a rumour becomes evidence without becoming a conviction by lunch.

choices.label: Sell your silence about the witness’s new hens

outcome.text: You receive fourteen gold. {{other}} retains the shaving and a particularly good description of the transaction.

charge.offence: Taking money to conceal church theft

title: THE SNARE HAS CAUGHT A FORESTER
text: {{other}} has trapped the forester’s leg in a snare meant for deer. The forester promises to be reasonable as soon as somebody stops being so criminally helpful.

choices.label: Cut the snare and give an honest account

outcome.text: The forester is freed and the trap is surrendered. {{other}} loses a valuable wire and gains a chance to explain it without a man screaming over the answer.

choices.label: Take the catch and leave the evidence

outcome.text: You carry away the meat. {{other}} can describe both your kindness and the direction in which it departed.

charge.offence: Taking game and abandoning a trapped forester

choices.label: Pay for help and surrender the poaching gear (8g)

outcome.text: You pay for care and the gear is taken as evidence. {{other}} discovers an unusually expensive method of catching no deer.

title: THE ALIBI WITH TOO MUCH DETAIL
text: {{other}} offers an alibi that includes the weather, the candles and what everyone ate. You remember only that you were not there for half of it.

choices.label: Give the part you actually know

outcome.text: The clerk crosses out an impressive meal and two useful hours. {{other}} has a weaker alibi and a witness who can survive a second question.

choices.label: Swear to the whole polished account

outcome.text: The first draft is still on the clerk’s desk. He puts it beside your oath and asks which version you would prefer to defend.

choices.label: Refuse to give evidence you cannot support

outcome.text: The court seeks another witness. {{other}} stops treating your presence as a thing that can be borrowed after the event.

title: THE COPE-CHEST HAS ACQUIRED A DEADLINE
text: {{other}} wants an oak chest, a lower price and an earlier delivery. The apprentice’s better joint is described as an unacceptable innovation until the old one splits.

choices.label: Use the apprentice’s joint and name the work honestly

outcome.text: The chest closes squarely. {{other}} tries to complain about the method and is defeated by the lid.

choices.label: Use cheap timber and conceal the split

outcome.text: You pocket the difference. {{other}} finds the split when the chest is lifted; the receipt is stronger than the wood.

choices.label: Return the advance rather than the promise (8g)

outcome.text: You return the advance and keep your tools. {{other}} takes the schedule to someone whose timber is apparently more obedient.

title: FOUR CARTS, ONE QUESTIONABLE GUARANTEE
text: {{other}} offers a place in a four-cart convoy. The safe-passage letter covers the road, the bridge and everything except the people collecting the toll.

choices.label: Pay for a clear shared contract (9g)

outcome.text: The hauliers sign the loss-sharing terms. {{other}} stops calling the profits guaranteed once somebody writes down who pays for a missing cart.

choices.label: Borrow for the unguarded shipment (30g debt)

success.text: The carts arrive and your return is paid. The loan also arrives, requiring rather less unloading.

failure.text: The goods are lost. Your creditor has stayed home and suffered no such misfortune.

choices.label: Keep your goods and refuse the guarantee

outcome.text: {{other}} offers three adjectives and no better security. You take your goods home before a fourth can be found.

title: THE WORKDAY THAT RAN INTO TOMORROW
text: {{other}} brings a contract requiring apprentices to work after the permitted hours. The master has solved the problem by describing midnight as late afternoon.

choices.label: Uphold the hours and take the smaller commission

outcome.text: You refuse the work that depends on the extra hours. {{other}} loses a commission and gains an example the apprentices can quote.

choices.label: Take the cheap work and break the agreed hours

outcome.text: You earn twelve gold. {{other}} submits the hours, which look much longer when laid beside your signature.

choices.label: Pay for food while the dispute is settled (8g)

outcome.text: The apprentices eat while the master finds a clock that agrees with the ordinance. {{other}} keeps the bread account separately from the speeches.

title: THE BUSHEL WITH LESS INSIDE THAN OUT
text: {{other}} presents a tithe measure with a handsome outside and a remarkably high bottom. The steward calls the difference ecclesiastical space.

outcome.text: You fill both measures from the same sack. {{other}} replaces the false one while explaining that certainty has become unpleasantly heavy.

choices.label: Pay to exempt your household alone (9g)

outcome.text: Your grain is spared and your neighbours’ grain is not. {{other}} keeps the payment in a box with a very accurate memory.
The new standard is kept in public. {{other}} dislikes the inconvenience of a bushel that does not improve when unattended.

title: THE LOTS ARE DRAWN BEFORE THE DRAWING
text: {{other}} brings a levy list containing the names of fourteen men. You were told there would be a drawing. The ink appears to have attended early.

choices.label: Demand a public drawing with exemptions read aloud

outcome.text: The list is remade before witnesses. {{other}} complains about delay while hiding the pen that predicted the first result.

choices.label: Pay for a lawful household exemption (14g)

outcome.text: The exemption is recorded and the levy continues. {{other}} gives you a receipt too large to hide in a sleeve.
The erased name leaves a fine white scar. {{other}} has the first copy, complete with a date that is not your friend.

title: TWO SEALS, NO CONFIDENCE
text: {{other}} brings two impressions of the guild seal. Both claim exclusive authority, and both smell of the same workshop.

choices.label: Compare the charter and lodge one public standard

outcome.text: You establish the authorised impression before the merchants. {{other}} must retire a very profitable second thumb.
The verification arrives with enough witnesses to outnumber the seals. {{other}} remarks that honesty is becoming expensive to counterfeit.
You collect sixteen gold and provide the guild with the only claim neither side wishes to defend.

title: THE THATCH HAS LEARNED THE WEATHER
text: {{other}} finds rot beneath your recently repaired roof. The repairer says it is not a leak if the water can also get out.

outcome.text: The rotten pieces come down and dry ones go up. {{other}} lets you count them before anybody describes the house as improved.

choices.label: Patch it with your own labour

outcome.text: You finish the patch with a stiff back and a dry bed. {{other}} tests the beam before congratulating you.

choices.label: Move the bowls and leave the repair

outcome.text: The bowls catch less than the rain brings. The household loses food and shelter while the repairer preserves a perfect record of having been paid.

title: THE RATS HAVE ACQUIRED A KEY
text: The granary sacks are light. {{other}} blames rats. You catch nine and find that the missing grain is still far too heavy for their combined ambition.

choices.label: Count the sacks and change the lock (5g)

outcome.text: The new lock excludes both the rats and the person who kept forgetting to report them. {{other}} loses the spare key with visible regret.

choices.label: Record an honest food allowance instead

outcome.text: The hungry household receives a proper ration. {{other}} signs for it; the sacks stop having to develop holes to feed somebody.

choices.label: Sell your silence about the missing sacks

outcome.text: You take eight gold from a theft that is still costing your household grain. {{other}} finds your arithmetic delightfully incurious.

charge.offence: Concealing theft from a communal granary

title: THE FIRE HAS NO RESPECT FOR BOUNDARIES
text: A neighbour’s roof burns and sparks reach your own thatch. {{other}} has a ladder, two buckets and an urgent theory about whose property matters first.

choices.label: Help the people before the property

success.text: You get the trapped household into the yard. {{other}} pours the last bucket on your sleeve and apologises for the part that was still warm.

failure.text: A falling spar burns your arm. You reach the yard alive, with pain that requires proper care.

outcome.text: Your roof survives. {{other}} watches where you pour the water and stops calling you neighbour quite so comfortably.
The crew passes water rather than opinions. {{other}} discovers how much quicker the work goes without deciding who deserves to be wet.

title: THE TREASURE MAP ENDS UNDER A BED
text: {{other}} sells a map to buried wealth. The last mark lies under a living neighbour’s bed. The map provides no advice about the neighbour.

choices.label: Ask permission and share any proceeds

outcome.text: The neighbour admits there is an old cellar and lets you inspect it. {{other}} looks disappointed that the first tool you used was a question.
The survey is genuine and the treasure annotation is newer. {{other}} lowers the price of the annotation without offering to improve the cellar.
You find a sound foundation and a furious owner. {{other}} declines to explain why you are under somebody’s floor.

charge.offence: Breaking into a dwelling to dig for treasure

title: THE BONE BOTH CHURCHES REMEMBER
text: {{other}} presents a relic claimed by two churches. Each can describe its miracles; neither can produce the receipt. The armed escort can produce several swords.

outcome.text: The inventory identifies the bone as a sheep’s. {{other}} asks whether that proves the sheep was not unusually devout.

choices.label: Sell the shrine’s display rights to both churches

outcome.text: You take sixteen gold and issue two incompatible promises. {{other}} places the contracts beside the bone, creating a rather better exhibit.

charge.offence: Selling conflicting rights to a disputed relic

outcome.text: The bone is catalogued without a procession. {{other}} laments the loss of a very profitable misunderstanding.

title: THE PROPHECY THAT HAS MET THE RENT
text: A child has made a striking prediction. {{other}} is charging to hear the next one and has begun suggesting that the heavens might be interested in this month’s rent.

choices.label: Stop the paying audience and hear the child quietly

outcome.text: Without the crowd, the prediction becomes a frightened child’s account of a flooded ditch. {{other}} has to find a different way to make it pay.

choices.label: Take a share of the prophecy takings

outcome.text: You receive fifteen gold. {{other}} adds another stool for paying customers, and the child learns which sort of answer brings supper.

choices.label: Pay for quiet care and food (8g)

outcome.text: The child gets food, a quiet room and an afternoon without questions. {{other}} receives a receipt instead of a revelation.

title: THE CHRISTENING SPOON IN THE WRONG SLEEVE
text: {{sibling}} has the household’s silver spoon and an explanation that grows more ancestral every time you ask.

choices.label: Ask for its return without an audience

outcome.text: The spoon comes home. {{sibling}} keeps the explanation, which is now too elaborate to throw away.

choices.label: Sell your claim for a fair payment

outcome.text: {{sibling}} pays five gold for the spoon and the right to stop describing your grandmother.

title: THE CARE AGREEMENT EVERYONE HAS HEARD ABOUT
text: {{other}} challenges a household care agreement. The dispute has attracted several people who have never provided any of the care.

choices.label: Read the actual terms before witnesses

outcome.text: The audience loses interest when the food, beds and responsibilities are counted. {{other}} signs the corrected terms instead of another accusation.

choices.label: Use the disagreement to humiliate the claimant

outcome.text: You win the audience and lose {{other}}’s trust. The people who offered no care offer excellent applause.

title: THE MIDWIFE ASKS FOR A HEARTH
text: {{other}} asks to use your main room for a birth. The floor is dry, the fire is good, and your household had other plans for both.

choices.label: Make room and provide clean fuel

outcome.text: You give up privacy and supplies. {{other}} moves the work indoors and leaves the arguments about inconvenience outside.
You fund a warm room nearby. {{other}} is grateful for an answer that includes a door which opens.

title: WHOSE NAME FITS ROUND THE BELL
text: {{other}} wants their name cast round a bell made by several hands. There is room for everyone’s mark, provided the patron’s titles lose a little weight.

choices.label: Credit the makers as well as the patron

outcome.text: The inscription becomes less flattering and more accurate. {{other}} objects to having neighbours in bronze.

choices.label: Reserve the whole inscription for the payer
