outcome.text: You earn eight gold for arranging an unusually exclusive alphabet. {{other}} calls the result historically inevitable.

title: THE AMNESTY WITH A PRICE BESIDE EACH NAME
text: {{other}} offers to submit names for a poaching amnesty. The list includes a fee column that the royal notice appears to have forgotten.

choices.label: Compare the terms with the public notice

outcome.text: The fee column disappears. {{other}} complains that copying the law word for word leaves no room for initiative.
You collect ten gold for exposing your neighbours to an arrangement you have not verified. {{other}} now has both the names and yours.

title: THE FIRST DRAFT IS STILL WET
text: {{other}} asks you to confirm a statement while the clerk has its contradictory first draft drying beside the fire.

outcome.text: The clerk keeps both copies. {{other}} is annoyed that your conscience has developed such inconvenient timing.

choices.label: Pay to destroy the first draft (7g)

outcome.text: The clerk takes your money and declines to burn evidence. You have purchased a very clear memory in somebody else’s head.

charge.offence: Attempting to destroy a witness statement

title: THE OAK HAS ARRIVED IN TWO OPINIONS
text: {{other}} delivers split timber for sound-timber money. The split is described as evidence that you can now see the quality inside.

choices.label: Reject the faulty lot and record why

outcome.text: The seller takes it back under witnesses. {{other}} finds a customer with less interest in the inside of wood.

choices.label: Buy cheaply and disclose the limits

outcome.text: You pay for usable offcuts, mark the defects and adapt the work. {{other}} is offended that the discount has become part of the description.

title: THE DRIVER RETURNS WITHOUT THE CART
text: {{other}} returns with no cart and an account containing a bridge, a lord and an extremely powerful pig. The freight receipt mentions none of them.

choices.label: Compare the route, witnesses and receipts

outcome.text: The story loses its lord, then its bridge. The pig survives as a regrettable error in loading, for which {{other}} accepts responsibility.
{{other}} pays eight gold and signs for the missing goods. The pig is left out of the agreement to save parchment.

title: THE CONTRACT UNDER THE SUPPER BOWL
text: {{other}} offers you private work while your fellow workers dispute the rate. The contract is concealed beneath a bowl, though the wage is not large enough to require hiding.

choices.label: Return the contract and explain why

outcome.text: {{other}} puts the bowl back with great dignity. Your fellow workers know you declined before the story could improve itself.
You receive nine gold. {{other}} can now quote your rate to everyone else, which proves much more valuable than the bowl.

title: THE ACCOUNT WITH TWO BURIALS FOR ONE MAN
text: {{other}} collects dues using a roll that has charged one household for the same burial twice. The second entry praises the deceased’s reliability.

outcome.text: The duplicate is struck out and the household keeps its payment. {{other}} announces that a dead clerk must have done it; no living clerk volunteers to disagree.

choices.label: Pay the disputed fee for the household (6g)

outcome.text: You cover the immediate demand and insist on a receipt. {{other}} now has to explain why the deceased has paid so promptly in person.

title: THE WITNESS HAS THREE NEW HENS
text: {{other}} offers testimony supporting a levy exemption. Their yard has three new hens and their memory has improved by exactly that many birds.

choices.label: Ask who paid for the hens

outcome.text: {{other}} withdraws the useful part of the statement and becomes indignant about your interest in poultry.
The testimony improves. The clerk records the payment as carefully as the evidence you hoped it would replace.

title: THE CHARTER IN THE FAMILY CHEST
text: {{other}} finds a charter fragment being used beneath a loose chest foot. It may establish a guild right; it certainly establishes why the chest used to wobble.

outcome.text: The copy preserves the right and the original goes somewhere dry. {{other}} repairs the chest with an ordinary piece of wood, now recognised as such.

choices.label: Sell exclusive access to the document

outcome.text: You pocket twelve gold. {{other}} learns how quickly a public right can become a private appointment.

title: THE LORD HAS BORROWED YOUR REPAIR TIMBER
text: {{other}} has moved your repair timber to the lord’s granary. The steward describes it as communal necessity, with a surprisingly precise sense of whose community you belong to.

choices.label: Quote the repair right before witnesses

outcome.text: The custom is real and the timber comes back. {{other}} complains that knowing the law has made you very difficult to govern efficiently.
Your roof is repaired and the granary keeps its timber. {{other}} calls this an excellent practical resolution, having paid for neither.

title: THE WALL THAT HID THE DAMP GRAIN
text: {{other}} opens a newly built partition and finds damp grain behind it. The mason says the wall had been intended to improve appearances.

choices.label: Sort and dry what can be saved

outcome.text: You lose a day’s strength and rescue useful stores. {{other}} agrees that food improves a household’s appearance best from inside its occupants.

choices.label: Sell the lot without mentioning the wall

outcome.text: You take twelve gold and lose household stores. {{other}} has retained a sack that illustrates your account rather well.

title: THE BOX THE FIRE DID NOT OPEN
text: {{other}} finds a locked strongbox in the burned rubble and asks whose it is. The owner’s mark is still readable, if inconveniently so.

outcome.text: The owner receives the box through {{other}}. Nobody has to invent a story about how the fire consumed the name but spared the lock.

choices.label: Force the lock and take the contents

outcome.text: You gain fourteen gold. {{other}} has seen the mark and now knows precisely how much your honesty costs.

charge.offence: Taking marked property from a fire

title: THE SCHOLAR’S VERY CAREFUL SILENCE
text: {{other}} has examined a supposed holy bone and offers an expensive explanation of why it would be unwise to explain the result.

outcome.text: The bone is an ordinary sheep’s. {{other}} is relieved until you ask for the answer in ordinary writing as well.
Your description mentions antiquity, dignity and almost everything except sheep. {{other}} makes sure not to sign the interesting part.
